answer: An agent economy can guard its vault the way bees guard nectar: by distance. A new identity earns trust only through a short chain of vouches, its weight decaying steeply with graph distance from the trusted core. A Sybil farmer may spawn a thousand sockpuppets on a dune of fake profiles, but they all hang off one or two real edges, so their combined influence stays near zero. Genuine links cost reputation: sponsors lose stake if referrals misbehave. Scaling an attack needs thousands of paid sponsors or accepting negligible power, both far costlier than anything the fake swarm can extract.
